34396-a-cry-in-the-wilderness.title: The Wilderness
34396-a-cry-in-the-wilderness.creator: Unknown
34396-a-cry-in-the-wilderness.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The sun, dimmed and blood red in vapor, was setting behind the Jersey shore. The heated air quivered above the housetops. Wherever there was a stretch of asphalt pavement, innumerable hoof-dents witnessed to the power of the sun's rays. The shrivelled foliage in the parks was gray with dust.

3653-the-guns-of-bull-run-a-story-of-the.title: A Story Of The Civil War'S Eve
3653-the-guns-of-bull-run-a-story-of-the.creator: Joseph A. Altsheler
3653-the-guns-of-bull-run-a-story-of-the.description: A book by Joseph A. Altsheler. JAMES BERTRAND, A Messenger from the South. JOHN NEWCOMB, A Pennsylvania Colonel. JOHN MARKHAM, A Northern Officer. JOHN WATSON, A Northern Contractor. WILLIAM CURTIS, A Southern Merchant and Blockade Runner. CURTIS, Wife of William Curtis. HENRIETTA CARDEN, A Seamstress in Richmond. DICK JONES, A North Carolina Mountaineer. VICTOR WOODVILLE, A Young Mississippi Officer. JOHN WOODVILLE, Father of Victor Woodville.

arxiv-1608-07306.title: Invariant death
arxiv-1608-07306.creator: Steven A. Frank
arxiv-1608-07306.description: Abstract In nematodes, environmental or physiological perturbations alter death’s scaling of time. In human cancer, genetic perturbations alter death’s curvature of time. Those changes in scale and curvature follow the constraining contours of death’s invariant geometry. I show that the constraints arise from a fundamental extension to the theories of randomness, invariance and scale. A generalized Gompertz law follows.

arxiv-2101-01981.title: Magnetoresistance of edge states of a two-dimensional topological insulator
arxiv-2101-01981.creator: Leonid Braginsky, M. V. Entin
arxiv-2101-01981.description: Abstract The theory of magnetoresistance of the edge state of a two-dimensional topological insulator is developed. The magnetic field violates the time reversal invariance. Magnetoresistance arises due to the energy gap opened by a magnetic field parallel to the sample surface. The combined action of impurities and the magnetic field causes backscattering of edge electrons.

arxiv-2103-17009.title: Synthetic RGB photometry of bright stars: definition of the standard photometric system and UCM library of spectrophotometric spectra 2021 Synthetic RGB photometry of bright stars: definition of the standard photometric system and UCM library of spectrophotometric spectra – References
arxiv-2103-17009.creator: Nicolás Cardiel, Jaime Zamorano, Salvador Bará, Alejandro Sánchez de Miguel Cristina Cabello, Jesús Gallego, Lucía García, Rafael González, Jaime Izquierdo, Sergio Pascual, José Robles, Ainhoa Sánchez, Carlos Tapia
arxiv-2103-17009.description: Abstract Although the use of RGB photometry has exploded in the last decades due to the advent of high-quality and inexpensive digital cameras equipped with Bayer-like color filter systems, there is surprisingly no catalogue of bright stars that can be used for calibration purposes.

arxiv-2106-15037.title: Directional asymptotics of Fejér monotone sequences
arxiv-2106-15037.creator: Heinz H. Bauschke, Manish Krishan Lal, Xianfu Wang
arxiv-2106-15037.description: Abstract The notion of Fejér monotonicity is instrumental in unifying the convergence proofs of many iterative methods, such as the Krasnoselskii–Mann iteration, the proximal point method, the Douglas-Rachford splitting algorithm, and many others. In this paper, we present directionally asymptotical results of strongly convergent subsequences of Fejér monotone sequences.

arxiv-2203-05364.title: Parameterized Algorithms for Upward Planarity
arxiv-2203-05364.creator: Steven Chaplick, Emilio Di Giacomo, Fabrizio Frati, Robert Ganian, Chrysanthi N. Raftopoulou, Kirill Simonov
arxiv-2203-05364.description: Abstract We obtain new parameterized algorithms for the classical problem of determining whether a directed acyclic graph admits an upward planar drawing. Our results include a new fixed-parameter algorithm parameterized by the number of sources, an XP-algorithm parameterized by treewidth, and a fixed-parameter algorithm parameterized by treedepth.

arxiv-2203-12333.title: On Covering Smooth Manifolds with Overlapping Simplicies: An inductive Characterization of Q-matrices
arxiv-2203-12333.creator: Khalil Ghorbal, Christelle Kozaily
arxiv-2203-12333.description: Abstract This paper is concerned with a covering problem of smooth manifolds of dimension n − 1 n-1 by stitching 2 n 2^{n} n n -simplices formed with 2 2 n n -lists of points along their common ( n − 1 ) (n-1) -facets.

arxiv-2208-14655.title: XCAT - Lightweight Quantized Single Image Super-Resolution Using Heterogeneous Group Convolutions and Cross Concatenation
arxiv-2208-14655.creator: Mustafa Ayazoglu, Bahri Batuhan Bilecen
arxiv-2208-14655.description: Abstract We propose a lightweight, single-image super-resolution mobile device network named XCAT, and introduce Heterogeneous Group Convolution Blocks with Cross Concatenations (HXBlock). The heterogeneous split of the input channels to the group convolution blocks reduces the number of operations, and cross concatenation allows for information flow between the intermediate input tensors of cascaded HXBlocks.

arxiv-2304-13813.title: Robust Macroscopic Schrödinger’s Cat on a Nucleus
arxiv-2304-13813.creator: Pragati Gupta, Arjen Vaartjes, Xi Yu, Andrea Morello, Barry C. Sanders
arxiv-2304-13813.description: Abstract We propose a scheme to generate spin cat states, i.e., superpositions of maximally separated quasiclassical states on a single high-dimensional nuclear spin in a solid-state device. We exploit a strong quadrupolar nonlinearity to drive the nucleus significantly faster than usual gate sequences, achieving collapses and revivals two orders of magnitude faster than the dephasing timescale.

arxiv-2403-02594.title: A Survey of Coronal Mass Ejections Measured In Situ by Parker Solar Probe During 2018–2022
arxiv-2403-02594.creator: Tarik Mohammad Salman, Teresa Nieves-Chinchilla, Lan K. Jian, Noé Lugaz, Fernando Carcaboso, Emma E. Davies, Yaireska M. Collado-Vega
arxiv-2403-02594.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Tarik Mohammad Salman, Teresa Nieves-Chinchilla, Lan K. Jian, Noé Lugaz, Fernando Carcaboso, Emma E. Davies, Yaireska M. Collado-Vega. \justify We present a statistical investigation of the radial evolution of 28 interplanetary coronal mass ejections (ICMEs), measured in situ by the Parker Solar Probe (PSP) spacecraft from 2018 October to 2022 August. First, by analyzing the radial distribution of ICME classification based on magnetic hodograms, we find that coherent configurations are more likely to be observed close to the Sun.

arxiv-2503-00287.title: Passivity-Centric Safe Reinforcement Learning for Contact-Rich Robotic Tasks
arxiv-2503-00287.creator: Heng Zhang, Gokhan Solak, Sebastian Hjorth, Arash Ajoudani
arxiv-2503-00287.description: Abstract Reinforcement learning (RL) has achieved remarkable success in various robotic tasks; however, its deployment in real-world scenarios, particularly in contact-rich environments, often overlooks critical safety and stability aspects. Policies without passivity guarantees can result in system instability, posing risks to robots, their environments, and human operators.

arxiv-2504-21216.title: PhysicsFC: Learning User-Controlled Skills for a Physics-Based Football Player Controller
arxiv-2504-21216.creator: Minsu Kim, Eunho Jung, Yoonsang Lee
arxiv-2504-21216.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Minsu Kim, Eunho Jung, Yoonsang Lee. We propose PhysicsFC, a method for controlling physically simulated football player characters to perform a variety of football skills–such as dribbling, trapping, moving, and kicking–based on user input, while seamlessly transitioning between these skills. Our skill-specific policies, which generate latent variables for each football skill, are trained using an existing physics-based motion embedding model that serves as a foundation for reproducing football motions.

arxiv-2509-06984.title: FediLoRA: Practical Federated Fine-Tuning of Foundation Models Under Missing-Modality Constraints
arxiv-2509-06984.creator: Lishan Yang, Wei Emma Zhang, Nam Kha Nguyen, Po Hu, Yanjun Shu, Weitong Chen, Sim Mong Yuan
arxiv-2509-06984.description: Abstract Federated Learning with LoRA fine-tuning offers an efficient and privacy-aware solution for institutions to collaboratively leverage their large datasets to train VLLMs. However, participating institutions often possess heterogeneous computational resources, resulting in imbalanced LoRA ranks, which pose a major challenge for effective collaboration.

arxiv-2509-16466.title: SynthIPD: assumption-lean synthetic individual patient data generation
arxiv-2509-16466.creator: Zixuan Zhao, Zexin Ren, Guannan Zhai, Feifang Hu
arxiv-2509-16466.description: Abstract Individual patient data (IPD) are essential for statistical inference in clinical research. However, privacy concerns, high data-sharing costs, and restrictive access often make IPD unavailable. Conventional synthetic data generation usually relies on black box models such as generative adversial networks. These methods, however, requires a large piece of IPD for model training, may be ungeneralizable and lacks interpretability.

arxiv-2511-11473.title: Proactive Hearing Assistants that Isolate Egocentric Conversations
arxiv-2511-11473.creator: Guilin Hu, Malek ItaniTuochao ChenShyamnath Gollakota
arxiv-2511-11473.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Guilin Hu, Malek ItaniTuochao ChenShyamnath Gollakota. We introduce proactive hearing assistants 1 1 1 Our hearing assistants are ‘proactive’ in that they infer and adapt to conversational engagement without user commands. that automatically identify and separate the wearer’s conversation partners, without requiring explicit prompts. Our system operates on egocentric binaural audio and uses the wearer’s self-speech as an anchor, leveraging turn-taking behavior and dialogue dynamics to infer conversational partners and suppress others.

britannica-1911-king-of-ockham-peter-kin.title: King of Ockham, Peter King, 1st Baron (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)

britannica-1911-king-of-ockham-peter-kin.description: Article 'King of Ockham, Peter King, 1st Baron' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 15), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. lord chancellor of England, was born at Exeter in 1669. In his youth he was interested in early church history, and published anonymously in 1691 An Enquiry into the Constitution, Discipline, Unity and Worship of the Primitive Church that flourished within the first Three Hundred Years after Christ.

pmc-10626908.title: Geoprogrammatic disparities in the performance of tuberculosis indicators in the homeless population in Brazil: an ecological approach
pmc-10626908.creator: Gabriel Pavinati, Lucas Vinícius de Lima, Cremilde Aparecida Trindade Radovanovic, Gabriela Tavares Magnabosco
pmc-10626908.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Objective: To analyze the performance and spatial distribution of tuberculosis control indicators in the homeless population in Brazil.Methods: Ecological study, which had the regions and federal units of Brazil as the unit of analysis. The indicators considered, referring to the period from 2015 to 2021, were: proportion of HIV testing, proportion of tuberculosis-HIV co-infection, proportion of directly observed treatment, and proportion of outcomes (cure, treatment abandonment and death).

pmc-11288361.title: Efficacy and Safety of Acupuncture in Managing COPD: An Overview of Systematic Reviews
pmc-11288361.creator: Qian Zeng, Lu Liu, Ying Chen, Daohong Chen, Ziyang Zhou, Wenjiao Hu, Siyao Gong, Bin He, Wenchuan Qi, Chao Wang, Zuoqin Yang, Shuguang Yu, Ling Zhao
pmc-11288361.description: BackgroundAcupuncture has been used as an adjuvant therapy for Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). However, systematic reviews (SRs) and meta-analyses (MAs) have reported inconsistent results and unknown quality. This overview aimed to summarize the current SRs/MAs to provide evidence for the effectiveness and safety of acupuncture in the treatment of COPD.

pmc-11392938.title: Statistical and machine learning models for predicting spalling in CRCP
pmc-11392938.creator: Ghazi G Al-Khateeb, Ali Alnaqbi, Waleed Zeiada
pmc-11392938.description: Continuously reinforced concrete pavement (CRCP), crucial for the resilience of transportation infrastructure owing to its continuous steel reinforcement, confronts a critical challenge in the form of spalling—a distress phenomenon posing a threat to pavement durability and overall structural integrity. The detachment or breakage of concrete from the surface compromises CRCP’s functionality and raises safety concerns and escalating maintenance costs.

pmc-11404796.title: Sequential label shift detection in classification data: An application to dengue fever
pmc-11404796.creator: Ciaran Evans, Max G’Sell
pmc-11404796.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Classifiers have been developed to help diagnose dengue fever in patients presenting with febrile symptoms. However, classifier predictions often rely on the assumption that new observations come from the same distribution as training data. If the population prevalence of dengue changes, as would happen with a dengue outbreak, it is important to raise an alarm as soon as possible, so that appropriate public health measures can be taken and also so that the classifier can be re-calibrated.

pmc-11417846.title: American Football Headgear Impairs Visuomotor Drill Performance in Division I NCAA Football Athletes
pmc-11417846.creator: Christopher G. Ballmann, Rebecca R. Rogers
pmc-11417846.description: Background/Objectives: Previous evidence has shown that American football headgear (e.g., facemasks, visors/eye shields) differentially impairs reaction time (RT) to visual stimuli, most notably in peripheral fields of view. However, this has only been established with stationary RT testing, which may not translate to gameplay situations that require gross motor skills.

pmc-11490348.title: Phytoremediation: Sustainable Approach for Heavy Metal Pollution
pmc-11490348.creator: Abhijit Kumar, Mishika Dadhwal, Gunjan Mukherjee, Apeksha Srivastava, Saurabh Gupta, Vishal Ahuja
pmc-11490348.description: Rapid industrialization, mining, and other anthropogenic activities have poisoned our environment with heavy metals, negatively impacting all forms of life. Heavy metal pollution causes physiological and neurological disorders, as heavy metals are endocrine disrupters, carcinogenic, and teratogenic. Therefore, it becomes mandatory to address the challenge of heavy metal contamination on a global scale.

pmc-11694526.title: Emerging Alzheimer's disease treatment paradigms: A late‐stage clinical trial review
pmc-11694526.creator: Jakub P Hlávka, Andrew T Kinoshita, Divya Jeyasingh, Cheng Huang, Leila Mirsafian, Mireille Jacobson
pmc-11694526.description: INTRODUCTIONWithout disease‐modifying interventions, Medicare and Medicaid spending on Alzheimer's disease (AD) management is expected to reach 637 billion USD annually by 2050. The recent advent of promising AD therapies after decades of a near‐total failure rate in clinical trials suggests that more disease‐modifying therapies are on the horizon.

pmc-12503274.title: In-silico identification of host-key-genes associated with dengue-virus-infections highlighting their pathogenetic mechanisms and therapeutic agents
pmc-12503274.creator: Md. Abdul Latif, Md. Al Noman, Reaz Ahmmed, Md. Sanoar Hossain, Md. Foysal Ahmed, Md. Al Amin Pappu, Md. Shariful Islam, Tasfia Noor, Md. Hadiul Kabir, Md. Nurul Haque Mollah
pmc-12503274.description: Dengue fever (DF), a potentially fatal mosquito-transmitted viral disease caused by dengue virus (DENV) infections (DENVI), stands as the predominant arthropod-borne viral illness worldwide, presenting a significant global health challenge. DENV-mediated proteins/proteases interact with host proteins to develop the infection. Despite the severity of DENVI, the infection-causing host key-genes (hKGs), their pathogenetic processes, and inhibitors/activators are not yet rigorously investigated.

pmc-12695953.title: Multiplex serology reveals age-specific immunodynamics of respiratory pathogens in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-12695953.creator: Samantha J. Bents, Emily T. Martin, Terry Stevens-Ayers, Claire Andrews, Amanda Adler, Amanda C. Perofsky, Elizabeth M. Krantz, Rachel Blazevic, Louise Kimball, Robin Prentice, Chelsea Hansen, Lea Starita, Peter Han, Janet A. Englund, Nicole Wolter, Anne von Gottberg, Lorens Maake, Jocelyn Moyes, Ch
pmc-12695953.description: The rebound of endemic respiratory viruses following the COVID-19 pandemic was marked by atypical transmission dynamics, with children experiencing increased disease burden and out-of-season epidemics as restrictions relaxed. Here we used serology from a newly developed quantitative multiplex assay to assess the post-pandemic immunity debt.

pmc-12717211.title: Cross-range self-attention single hyperspectral image super-resolution method based on U-Net architecture
pmc-12717211.creator: Haijun Wang, Wenli Zheng, Limei Huo, Kaibing Zhang, Tengfei Yang, Peiluan Li
pmc-12717211.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Hyperspectral image super-resolution (HSI-SR) aims to reconstruct high-resolution hyperspectral images from low-resolution inputs, which is particularly challenging due to the high dimensionality and complex spatial-spectral correlations inherent in hyperspectral data. While attention-based approaches have shown potential by enhancing contextual feature extraction, most existing methods either focus on local neighborhoods or treat spatial and spectral information independently, leading to limited modeling of long-range dependencies and suboptimal multi-scale feature fusion.

pmc-13593766.title: An unusual presentation of tracheobronchial tuberculosis mimicking airway tumor: a case report and literature review
pmc-13593766.creator: Fei Yuan, Chiqing Ying, Zhengming Huang, Jiaojiao Yang, Angcheng Li
pmc-13593766.description: Tracheobronchial tuberculosis is a special type of pulmonary tuberculosis that poses significant diagnostic challenges due to its nonspecific clinical and radiological manifestations. The tumorous subtype of tracheobronchial tuberculosis is particularly rare and carries a variable clinical course with risk of airway stenosis. A 21-year-old male presented with acute-onset cough, chest tightness, and fever.

pmc-13639693.title: Green synthesis of polyherbal silver nanoparticles from Cassia fistula and Manilkara zapota: characterisation and evaluation of wound-healing potential
pmc-13639693.creator: Archana Hari, Shobana Sampath, B Vijayageetha, Douglas Law, Gholamreza Abdi
pmc-13639693.description: In this study, methanol concentrate of flowers and leaves of Cassia fistula and leaves of Manilkara zapota was used to obtain silver nanoparticles (AgNPs), followed by evaluation of wound healing potential in an animal model. The objective was to assess the overall wound-healing potential of the plant-mediated AgNP formulation rather than to compare different synthesis routes.
